title: From Shots to Forecasts: One-Step-Ahead Prediction of Team-Level Expected Goals in Football
content: Expected goals (xG) describe football performance, but their value as time-series signals for forecasting future team performance is less established. We evaluated one-step-ahead team-level xG forecasts using 32,121 matches from 30 competitions and chronological training, validation, and test periods defined within each competition--season. The primary target was focal-team xG (\( \mathrm{xG}^{F} \)); xG against (\( \mathrm{xG}^{A} \)) and xG difference (\( \mathrm{xG}^{D} \)) were derived from paired team forecasts. We compared rolling mean, ARIMA, linear mixed-effects, XGBoost, and Temporal ConvNet models. On the held-out test set, the mixed-effects model achieved the lowest MAE for \( \mathrm{xG}^{F} \)(0.545 versus 0.591 for the rolling benchmark) and \( \mathrm{xG}^{D} \) (0.790 versus 0.861). XGBoost had similar MAE and the highest \( \mathrm{xG}^{D} \) directional accuracy (66.35\%). Paired bootstrap inference showed improvements over the rolling benchmark for the mixed-effects model, XGBoost, and Temporal ConvNet, but not ARIMA. XGBoost also outperformed the rolling benchmark in all 30 leave-one-competition-out evaluations. However, adding recent xG-history features to team, opponent, competition, season, and venue information did not produce a statistically detectable reduction in test-set MAE. Under matched information, XGBoost and the Temporal ConvNet had numerically similar MAE. These results support structured panel forecasting but indicate limited incremental MAE value from recent xG history in this retrospective within-panel design.
